text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 1.85% today to $396.11, building on a 9.27% gain over the past two weeks. The immediate driver is a sharp rise in oil prices—Brent crude hit $98 a barrel today after attacks on Saudi energy facilities by Iran-aligned Houthis, combined with recent U.S.-Iran military exchanges. Higher crude prices improve refiner margins (the profit refiners make by turning crude into gasoline and diesel), and U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity, positioning the company to capture that margin expansion.

The broader tailwind is Middle East geopolitical tension. Whenever supply disruption risks spike in that region, oil prices typically rise, which benefits refiners with the spare capacity to run hard and sell products at better prices. Storage levels for both gasoline and diesel remain moderate, leaving room for demand without oversupply dampening margins further.
